All 8 items are fixed in 6 commits on top of bdba3c69. Nothing is left uncommitted and nothing was pushed. The web typecheck and lint gates both pass; lint shows 2 warnings, both in files outside this stream. No tests were run, as instructed.

N-30 was the blocker. The API builds templates with Go's html/template, which needs `{{.name}}`. The editor was matching, inserting and previewing `{{name}}`, which the API cannot parse. A new module, apps/web/features/documents/template-syntax.ts, now handles this syntax:
- It reads `{{...}}` actions, including spaces, the `{{- ` / ` -}}` whitespace-trim markers and comments.
- It tracks what the dot refers to inside range, with and if blocks.
- It lists the values the body uses, which drives both the 'Data otomatis yang dipakai' summary and the `variables` sent on save.
- It finds old `{{name}}` placeholders and adds the missing dot (`fixLegacyPlaceholders`).
- It draws the preview with each value shown as its label in square brackets, and draws a list block once.

Insert chips now write `{{.name}}`. The leave letter has the API's full list of 15 values. Warning letters and visitor badges are also printed from the school's own template, so they now get their own values too, plus a 'Daftar pelanggaran' chip that inserts a range block.

Decision on templates saved with the old syntax: they are flagged, not converted on load. The body opens exactly as saved, and a warning Alert offers 'Perbaiki format', which adds the dots. Saving is refused while any old-format placeholder remains, with a message under the field. The template list shows a 'Perlu diperbaiki' badge on any such template. The test files cover the parser, the fix-up, the preview, inserting values, the old-format flow and the preview sheet.

units.verdict:
Does it look very professional? Mostly yes. I looked at about 60 images: the 13 sweep pairs, the 8 extra shots, the home page of all nine roles on phone and desktop, sign-in in light and dark, lists (users, catalogue, rules, early warning, leave requests), detail and form screens (student, library member, catalogue title, supervision observation, template editor, new-year wizard), settings (index, brand, roles, notifications), and 10 dark shots. The shell, type scale, cards, stat strips, list rows, empty states and the green palette now hold together on every screen. Dark mode is as finished as light. The sign-in page is polished. Nothing I saw is broken. Of the 13 pairs, 8 improved and 5 changed neutrally (mostly data); none regressed.

Does it read as one product? Yes. All nine roles get the same home: a hero card, then a figure strip, then the work check-in card and the role's own cards. Every list uses the same header, tab strip, filter pills and table or card list. Detail pages share the avatar-led title. The seams that remain are small: the phone primary action now comes in two forms, and the early-warning page uses tiles on a phone where the other pages use the strip.

Does it feel like a phone app on a phone? Largely yes. There is a bottom tab bar with a raised centre action for each role, round title-row actions, bottom-sheet dialogs with sticky Batal and Simpan, segmented controls, filter pills, a sticky save bar and stacked full-width actions on the state pages. A few desktop habits remain: a labelled pill button sits under the title on most list pages, the catalogue title page has a "Pilih semua baris" checkbox list, and the template body is raw HTML.

Five weakest things left, in order:
1. On a phone, today's notification rows show "18 menit yang lalu" in the trailing slot, which cuts titles to "Pengajuan izin di…". Everyone sees this every day.
2. Rows filled in from a leave letter put English machine text, "leave letter 21/IZIN/XI/2026", into a teacher's attendance note.
3. The phone primary action has two forms. Eight pages use a round "+" beside the title; users, catalogue, journal, title detail and duty keep the green labelled pill under the title.
4. A fresh school's home is a stack of placeholders. The work check-in card now sits second or third on every staff phone home, showing dashes and "Jadwal belum diatur". The library home stacks two figure grids, 11 numbers, before any content.
5. The document template editor is still a raw HTML textarea for school admins. On a phone, its new Pratinjau button squeezes the card description into a narrow 4-line column.

None of these is a blocker or a second-pass regression. Items 1 and 2 are quick fixes worth doing before hand-over if time allows.

Overall score: 8. It is professional, with small blemishes. It is not yet a 9: the remaining issues are visible on the most-used screens (notifications, attendance, the homes), and two phone patterns still disagree.

units.verdict: The pass worked for almost everything. 31 of the 35 items are fixed or confirmed in code, and N-30 is solid on the web side. The template editor now writes {{.name}} and lists the same values the API passes for leave letters (all 15), warning letters and visitor badges; I checked these against leaverequest.go:389-395, discipline letters.go:139-144 and visitors visits.go:104-106. The preview shows readable labels in brackets ([Nama siswa]) and the 'Data otomatis yang dipakai' badges are filled. Templates saved in the old {{name}} form are flagged in the editor and on the list page, and they cannot be saved until fixed. The only gap in N-30 is the API-side check: apps/api was not touched, so a body with any other syntax error still saves and makes every letter of that kind fail to issue. That is a hardening follow-up, not a blocker. There is one clear regression to fix now. R-FA-22 moved the desk's overdue queue into the narrow left column. The overdue table no longer fits there: its 'Kembalikan' buttons and row menus are clipped off the card's right edge, and member names break into four or five lines. Everything else that was asked is visible on the new photographs: the home pages no longer repeat facts; the supervision icon row is gone; the Buku tamu and Presensi tab rows stay at one height; the promotion card has a proper header; the kiosk fits a phone; the catalogue-data select works; the setup checklist rows read in full; and the compact '+' action shows on the five listed pages. Of the issues found with fresh eyes, only the desk is serious. The rest are minor or polish.
